prompt: A children's board-game teaching diagram shows a single looped track of 24 numbered squares (0 to 23) around the edge of the board. MY red token starts on square 3. An opponent's blue token sits on square 14 and never moves on its own. I roll the die three times in a row and move my red token forward by that many squares each time: first I roll 5, then 4, then 2. If my red token ever LANDS exactly on the opponent's square, the opponent's blue token is CAPTURED and sent off the track (removed), while my red token stays on that square. Work the three moves forward and render the board's FINAL state: place MY red token on its final square, and show the blue token only if it was NOT captured. Do NOT print the die rolls or the square number of my token anywhere on the board.
